newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks slump late on profit-taking and Dow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks slump late on profit-taking and Dow.

text.p: Mexican stocks shied away from resistance and pared earlier gains to close lower for the first time this week on Thursday, as dealers took profits on cue from the slide in Dow Industrials, traders said.

"The Dow Jones dragged us down, and people are awaiting trade balance figures tomorrow," said an equity analyst. "Furthermore, the resistance at 3,400 points is becoming a tough psychological barrier."
The IPC closed down 7.45 points, or 0.22 percent, at 3,365.35. Trade figures were held to be important as they give a guide to whether the peso is correctly valued, traders said.
The IPC reached an early high of 3,392.59 points, before the downward trend of the Dow took effect.
Some traders said the market was still being buttressed by a favorable outlook for forthcoming earnings reports.
"I still like the market. Prices are low and bottom fishers are waiting for them to get a bit lower," said a trader.
On the broad market, 106 shares were traded, of which losers outnumbered winners by 46 to 43. Volume was reasonable at 84.2 million shares traded, and up from earlier sessions this week.

Hard-hit autoparts maker Iasasa A series shares headed the percentage gainers after a technical rebound, whereas its B series shares headed the losers. The A series closed up three centavos to 20 centavos, while the b series closed down eighjt centavos to 46 centavos.

"Iasasa's problem is its contradictory situation. It trades in a vigorous sector and its operations are fine, but its short-term debts are heavy. Investors seemed to acknowledge that (the A series) had been hit too hard, while the B series is still adjusting," an equity analyst said.
